thread:
incident-bot: INCIDENT ALERT: elevated p99 latency + token inflation on /v1/chat (hosted:dense-x). Paging on-call. Please ack. :rotating_light:

sam: acked. seeing a big spike in KV cache size on runtime-pool-17, memory pressure + GC thrash. CPU on those hosts jumped to ~95%.

jules: logs show a surge of unique prefix keys starting ~1769998600, very uneven distribution. snippet:```
[1769998612] kv_store.insert key=prompt_cache:sha1:9f8a... size=12345
[1769998612] kv_store.insert key=prompt_cache:6a7b... size=12001
[1769998613] kv_store.size=18734234 entries
```

livia: looks like a key explosion rather than steady growth. any recent changes to tokenizer or prompt templates?

morgan: rolled model bundle redwood/open-x/2026-03-09 at 1769994000 that included a tokenizer fix + a prompt templating tweak in the SDK. Could be related.

sam: correlating: the first big jump in unique keys aligns with the client-side template change we shipped yesterday (template now injects user.locale earlier). That can change prefix hashes if hashing order isn't stable.

jules: also noticing continuous batching *coalescer* config is hitting extreme batch sizes, so single requests are aggregating many unique prefixes and causing KV cache to warm up massively per batch. Perf cliff when cache misses + huge KV writes.

ryan-oncall: taking ownership for mitigation. immediate actions?

morgan: recommend these steps now (hotfix path):
1) disable continuous batching on hosted pool (temporary)
2) clear prefix/prompt cache for affected runtime pool scope
3) rollback template change in SDK or deploy a compat shim that normalizes prompt ordering
4) throttle concurrent warmup to avoid spike

livia: commands for 1) and 2():```bash
# disable continuous batching on pool 17
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN" \n  https://console.internal.redwood/api/pools/17/config \n  -d '{"continuous_batching": false}'

# flush prompt cache for pool 17 (careful: scope=pool)
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN" \n  https://console.internal.redwood/admin/kv/flush \n  -d '{"scope":"pool:17","prefix":"prompt_cache"}'
```

sam: running flush now.

[deploy-bot]: start canary deploy for config-change/disable-batching -> pool-17

sam: disable continuous_batching pushed, canary started. monitoring.

jules: after flush we saw KV entries drop from 18M -> 120k over ~40s. CPU settled down to ~45%. p99 improved but some residual errors. logs:```
[1769998745] kv_store.size=120134
[1769998750] p99_latency=220ms (was 1.8s)
```

customer-ops: quick impact summary for postmortem: 23 active customers hit elevated latencies, 5 customers saw request errors (5xx) for ~6 minutes. no data loss reported. affected customers largely on dedicated pools in us-west-2.

ryan-oncall: good work. next: identify root cause. initial hypothesis: prompt hashing algorithm assumed deterministic tokenization order; SDK template change injected locale early which reordered tokens -> different prefix hashes -> cache miss on identical logical prompt -> mass insertions as batches warmed distinct new keys. Combined with continuous batching these misses amplified write load and GC.

livia: confirming tokenizer mismatch: token counts differ between old and new tokenizer for same input. diff:```
old_tokens = ["Hello","\n","{{user}}","!"]
new_tokens = ["Hello","\n","en-US","{{user}}","!"]
```
hashing code path hashed raw tokens list. We didn't canonicalize template variables insertion points.

morgan: also found a concurrent regression in the batching heuristics: when batch size > 256 unique prefixes, the runtime used a fallback path that didn't stream KV writes, causing a memory spike. we need to add guardrails.

sam: propose immediate follow-ups (post-incident):
- roll SDK template change back within 48h or ship a normalization shim
- add a pre-hash normalization function to runtime that strips or canonicalizes transient template vars (locale, timestamps)
- add protective limit: if unique_prefix_count_in_batch > 128, cap batch and flush incremental to avoid write storm
- add monitoring alert for prefix-key growth rate (sustained > 100k new keys/min)

jules: creating incident ticket and assigning owners. postmortem owner: livia. mitigation owner (hotfixes/rollouts): morgan.

customer-ops: messaging draft for customers affected: short summary + mitigation + ETA for full fix. will coordinate with sales for enterprise impacted accounts.

ryan-oncall: handing off to morgan for next 6 hours. I'll stay available for escalation. documenting handoff: current mitigation applied (continuous batching disabled, prefix cache flushed, canary stable). Next action: deploy batch cap + runtime pre-hash normalization in canary tomorrow morning.

morgan: acked, taking over. adding a safety throttle to runtime (PR now drafting).

[deploy-bot]: canary config-change/disable-batching -> pool-17 succeeded.

incident-bot: incident status: mitigated -> workaround in place. Severity lowered to S2. Logging this thread.

sam: thanks everyone. final notes: no customer data exposure. estimated cost impact: spike in backend writes for ~12 minutes, cloud bill delta minor but operational impact for some customers. planned follow-ups scheduled in the triage meeting tomorrow 13:00 UTC.

livia: will own RCA write-up and include timeline + code pointers. please add any logs or snippets here.

morgan: quick reminder: when re-enabling continuous batching, we need a gradual ramp (10% -> 50% -> 100%) and monitor unique prefix churn metric closely.

ryan-oncall: leaving thread but reachable. good handoff. :white_check_mark:

customer-ops: will send customer notes within 90m.

[END THREAD]
